**Yes, for the matching panel.** The text (page 2) says a pan-genome analysis of 45 isolates found 19,469 total genes, with 3,155 (~16.2%) core genes. Fig. 2E (page 4) has a panel labelled "Eduardo et al. 2019" showing Core (>95%) = 3,155, Dispensable = 7,847, and Unique = 8,467. These sum to 19,469, and 3,155 / 19,469 ≈ 16.2%, so the figure matches the text.

The other two panels in Fig. 2E (Danesh et al. 2016 and Filip et al. 2018) are different datasets and are not meant to match the 19,469 total. Their totals are about 13,587 and 16,456, respectively, based on the bar labels. The text attributes the 45-isolate analysis to reference [44], and the figure does not state an isolate count.
